questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated (id, title, description, keywords, license).
questions.evidence: id: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; title: 'Artificial Intelligence Ready and Equitable Atlas for Diabetes Insights (AI-READI)'; description: ~1,100 char narrative; keywords: 19 entries; license_and_use_terms: detailed CC BY-NC 4.0 + AI-READI Data License block
questions.quality_note: All five mandatory fields populated with substantive, high-quality content (100% populated).

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields (description, motivation) have meaningful content length.
questions.evidence: description field is ~1,100 characters; motivation captured via purposes (3 entries, each 200+ char descriptions, e.g. 'Better understand salutogenesis (the pathway from disease to health) in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus using a hypothesis-agnostic, harmonized, multi-domain dataset...')
questions.quality_note: Both description and motivation narratives far exceed 200 characters with rich, context-laden prose.

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords provided to describe dataset topic coverage.
questions.evidence: 19 unique keywords including 'Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus', 'Machine Learning', 'multimodal dataset', 'harmonized data', 'multi-site study', 'salutogenesis', 'retinal imaging', 'continuous glucose monitoring', 'biospecimens', 'triple-balanced sampling', 'health equity', 'Bridge2AI'
questions.quality_note: 19 diverse, well-targeted keywords spanning domain, methodology, and modality — greatly aids discoverability.

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
questions.description: Number of files and file type diversity in distribution_formats or files.listing.
questions.evidence: distribution_formats lists DICOM (imaging), CSV (tabular/time-series), mHealth standard (wearable), XML (ECG); distributions add ZIP archive packaging (application/zip). At least 4 distinct data formats plus container format.
questions.quality_note: Four+ distinct file/data formats reflecting genuinely multimodal data, exceeding the >3 threshold.

questions.name: Data File Size Availability
questions.description: Presence of file size or dimensional metadata (e.g., 513×N spectrogram).
questions.evidence: Sample/dimensional counts present: 'Target enrollment is 4,000 people'; ~1,000 participants per subpopulation (25% of sample); 'Blood (53 mL) and urine'; CGM 'every 5 minutes for 10 days'; environmental sensor '11 measurements'
questions.quality_note: Pass — dimensional/sample-count metadata (participant counts, sampling intervals, volumes) are present, though byte-level file sizes are not stated.

questions.name: Dataset Identification Metadata
questions.description: Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs.
questions.evidence: doi: 10.57895/fairhub.2; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; additional persistent DOIs in external_resources (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10642459, BMJ Open 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449)
questions.quality_note: Pass — a resolvable dataset DOI plus persistent landing-page URL are present.

questions.name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
questions.description: Presence of funding sources, grants, or institutional sponsors.
questions.evidence: funders: 'NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program... grant OT2OD032644, administered by NIH Office of the Director. Additional support from grants P30DK035816..., UL1TR003096, and Research to Prevent Blindness. Total funding in 2022: $5,026,499. Opportunity Number: OTA-21-008.'
questions.quality_note: Comprehensive: named agency, primary and supplementary award numbers, dollar amount, opportunity number, and acknowledgment of additional sponsors.

questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
questions.description: Presence of deidentification methods, IRB approvals, or ethical sourcing notes.
questions.score_label: IRB approval + deidentification + ethical sourcing details
questions.evidence: ethical_reviews: 'University of Washington (approval number STUDY00016228), with reliance agreements from IRBs of University of Alabama at Birmingham and University of California, San Diego'; is_deidentified: public dataset de-identified with sensitive PHI moved to controlled access; informed_consent and at_risk_populations (Community Advisory Board of 11, pregnancy exclusion) documented
questions.quality_note: Exemplary ethics coverage: specific IRB protocol number, reliance agreements, de-identification methodology, informed consent, and equitable/ethical sourcing via bioethics guidance and advisory board.

questions.name: Access Requirements Documentation
questions.description: Whether access policy and license are clearly defined (open, registered, restricted).
questions.score_label: License + Data Use Agreement + platform access description
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms: CC BY-NC 4.0 for public data; 'Controlled access data requires a separate data use agreement with the University of Washington as Licensor'; distributions describe public vs controlled ZIP archives at https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; access 'managed by the Data Access Committee'
questions.quality_note: Fully specified two-tier access: open license path, DUA-gated controlled tier, named governing committee, and platform download portal.

questions.name: Interoperability and Standardization
questions.description: Presence of standard formats, ontologies, or schema conformance.
questions.evidence: preproc: 'All data mapped to applicable data standard formats such as Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model for clinical data and DICOM format for retinal imaging'; medications coded with RxNorm; ICD-10 codes (E11.X, R73.09); wearable data converted to mHealth standard; follows FAIR principles
questions.quality_note: Strong interoperability: standard formats (DICOM, CSV, XML, mHealth) plus explicit standards/ontologies (OMOP CDM, RxNorm, ICD-10) and FAIR conformance.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.description: Mentions of preprocessing libraries or tools used in data preparation.
questions.score_label: At least one preprocessing tool listed
questions.evidence: REDCap named as data capture/management system; MoCA Duo Application (iPad) named; format-conversion steps documented ('.fda, .sdt) to DICOM', '.FIT format to mHealth standard'); instruments named (Dexcom G6, Garmin VivoSmart 5, Philips Pagewriter TC30)
questions.quality_note: Preprocessing/data-management tools (REDCap, MoCA app) and conversion pipelines are named, but no dedicated software_and_tools inventory with version numbers or URLs — limits full reproducibility.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.description: Description completeness of participant recruitment and data acquisition.
questions.score_label: Full recruitment and procedural details included
questions.evidence: collection_mechanisms detail EHR screening (ICD-10 E11.X/R73.09, ages 40+, 2020-2025), wave-based recruitment (enrollment began July 18, 2023), in-person visits (2.5-4 hours, 3 sites), home wearable monitoring (10-day), biospecimen collection (53 mL blood); 12 acquisition_methods; data_collectors describe certified coordinators following a Manual of Procedures
questions.quality_note: Outstanding procedural detail across recruitment, screening, sampling, in-person acquisition, and home monitoring.

questions.name: Version History Documentation
questions.description: Presence of multiple version records and associated dates.
questions.score_label: ≥2 versions with change summaries and release dates
questions.evidence: distribution_dates and updates: 'pilot data released May 2024; v1.0.0 data (through July 31, 2024) released November 2024; Versions 2.0.0 and 3.0.0 released with additional participants'; version_access: 'semantic versioning (e.g., v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0)... Each version includes a changelog and data dictionary'
questions.quality_note: Four release milestones with dates, participant-scope change summaries, and semantic-versioning/changelog governance.

questions.name: Associated Publications
questions.description: Presence of formal citations or DOI-linked references.
questions.score_label: Multiple references and dataset DOI cross-links
questions.evidence: external_resources cite 'Protocol Publication (BMJ Open)... (Owsley et al. 2025) at https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449', 'Nature Metabolism Commentary... https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x', and Zenodo archive https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10642459; dataset DOI 10.57895/fairhub.2 provides cross-linking
questions.quality_note: Multiple DOI-linked publications plus dataset DOI enable bidirectional cross-referencing, though these live under external_resources rather than a dedicated citations field.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.description: Inclusion of human subjects, demographic diversity, or subgroup details.
questions.evidence: instances: participants aged 40+, target 4,000, 'triple-balanced by self-reported race/ethnicity (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White), T2DM severity..., and biological sex'; 8 subpopulations with ~1,000-participant targets each; inclusion (English-speaking, 40+) and exclusion (pregnancy, type 1 diabetes) criteria stated
questions.quality_note: Rich demographic characterization with explicit subgroup targets and inclusion/exclusion criteria.

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Dataset includes persistent URLs for access and documentation.
questions.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; external_resources include https://aireadi.org/, https://docs.aireadi.org/, https://bridge2ai.org/, https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10471118, and DOI-based persistent links
questions.quality_note: Pass — multiple persistent, resolvable URLs for access and documentation.

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.description: Describes how users can obtain the dataset (download, DUA, login).
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path (platform, login, policy)
questions.evidence: 'Public access subset... available at https://fairhub.io/datasets/2 upon agreement with the CC BY-NC 4.0 license'; 'Controlled access subset requiring a data use agreement... managed by the Data Access Committee'; distributed as ZIP archives
questions.quality_note: Access path fully described: platform portal, license agreement for open tier, DUA and governing committee for controlled tier.

questions.name: Reusability (License Clarity)
questions.description: License is clearly defined and permits identifiable reuse cases.
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms: CC BY-NC 4.0 'Permits others to distribute, remix, adapt, build upon this work non-commercially... provided the original work is properly cited, appropriate credit is given, any changes made indicated, and the use is non-commercial'; explicit prohibitions on clinical decisions, re-identification, and non-licensed sharing
questions.quality_note: License and reuse conditions are explicit, including permitted derivative use and clearly stated restrictions.

questions.name: Data Integrity and Provenance
questions.description: Presence of change logs or provenance tracking.
questions.evidence: version_access: 'All prior versions... maintained with version-specific documentation at https://docs.aireadi.org/. Each version includes a changelog and data dictionary. Dataset versioning uses semantic versioning'; updates lists dated releases (May 2024, November 2024, v2.0.0/v3.0.0)
questions.quality_note: Structured semantic versioning with changelogs, dated releases, and retained prior versions constitutes strong provenance tracking.

questions.name: Interlinking Across Platforms
questions.description: Metadata connects dataset records across multiple platforms.
questions.evidence: external_resources link FAIRhub (https://fairhub.io/datasets/2), Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10642459), NIH RePORTER (https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10471118), Bridge2AI (https://bridge2ai.org/), and project/docs sites
questions.quality_note: Pass — dataset record is interlinked across FAIRhub, Zenodo, NIH RePORTER, and program/project platforms.

strengths: Complete structural metadata: all mandatory fields populated with substantive content, 19 keywords, and 4+ distinct distribution formats
Exemplary ethics and privacy documentation including specific IRB protocol (STUDY00016228), reliance agreements, de-identification methodology, informed consent, and a Community Advisory Board
Comprehensive funding detail with agency, primary/supplementary award numbers, dollar amount, and opportunity number
Strong FAIR compliance: dataset DOI, persistent landing pages, semantic versioning with changelogs, and cross-platform interlinking (FAIRhub, Zenodo, NIH RePORTER)
Outstanding collection-protocol clarity spanning EHR screening, wave-based recruitment, 12 acquisition methods, and standardized coordinator procedures
Robust interoperability via standard formats (DICOM, mHealth) and standards/ontologies (OMOP CDM, RxNorm, ICD-10)
weaknesses: No dedicated software_and_tools inventory; named tools (REDCap, MoCA Duo App) lack version numbers or repository/URL links, limiting full reproducibility
Byte-level file sizes are absent (only participant counts, sampling intervals, and volumes are given)
Associated publications are embedded in external_resources rather than a structured citations/references field
recommendations: Add a software_and_tools section enumerating preprocessing/conversion software with version numbers and URLs (e.g., the .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM and .FIT-to-mHealth conversion utilities, REDCap version)
Include approximate file/archive sizes or per-modality dimensional metadata (e.g., image counts, array shapes) to aid download planning
Promote the BMJ Open, Nature Metabolism, and Zenodo references into a dedicated citations field with formal citation strings alongside their DOIs
